subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Welford's information-processing model, the perceptual mechanism is responsible for:
options: Interpreting and making sense of the display
questions.explain: The perceptual mechanism interprets and gives meaning to the information received from the display.

questions.q: Which is one of Bandura's four sources of self-efficacy?
questions.explain: Performance accomplishments (past success) are the strongest source of self-efficacy in Bandura's model.

questions.q: In Fiedler's contingency model, a task-oriented leader is most effective when the situation is:
questions.explain: Fiedler suggests task-oriented leaders are most effective in the most and least favourable situations.

questions.q: In Weiner's attribution model, ability is classified as which type of attribution?
questions.explain: In Weiner's model, ability is an internal (locus of causality) and stable factor.

questions.q: The frustration-aggression hypothesis proposes that aggression results when:
questions.explain: The frustration-aggression hypothesis states blocked goals create frustration which leads to aggression.

questions.q: Which guidance type is most useful for a beginner learning a dangerous skill?
questions.explain: Manual/mechanical guidance physically supports the learner, aiding safety and confidence in dangerous skills.

questions.q: The presence of an audience improving the performance of a well-learned skill is termed:
questions.explain: Social facilitation is the positive effect of an audience on the performance of well-learned skills.

questions.q: In schema theory, knowledge of the conditions and environment before a movement is the:
questions.explain: Initial conditions provide information about the environment and body position before the movement.

questions.q: The tendency for individuals to reduce effort when performing within a group is called:
questions.explain: Social loafing is the reduction of individual effort within a group, linked to the Ringelmann effect.

questions.q: In the triadic model, an attitude's emotional component is the:
questions.explain: The affective component reflects the feelings and emotions a person holds towards an attitude object.

questions.q: Practising a whole skill broken into parts that are then combined is known as:
questions.explain: Progressive-part practice teaches parts separately then links them progressively into the whole.

questions.q: Goals based on improving on one's own previous standards are described as:
questions.explain: Performance goals focus on personal standards and improvement rather than the result against others.

questions.q: A skill whose timing and pace are controlled by the performer is classified as:
questions.explain: In self-paced (internally paced) skills the performer determines when the movement starts and its rate.

questions.q: The inverted-U theory predicts optimal performance occurs at:
questions.explain: The inverted-U theory states performance is best at a moderate, optimal level of arousal.

questions.q: The short-term memory is often described as having a capacity of approximately:
options: 7 plus or minus 2 items for up to 30 seconds
questions.explain: Short-term memory holds about 7 plus or minus 2 items for roughly 30 seconds unless rehearsed.

questions.q: Which practice type is most suitable for grooving a closed skill in a stable environment?
questions.explain: Fixed (drill) practice repeats a skill in the same way, ideal for grooving stable closed skills.

questions.q: The transfer of a skill from one limb to the opposite limb is termed:
questions.explain: Bilateral transfer is the transfer of learning from one side of the body to the other.

questions.q: A skill performed in a stable, predictable environment that is unaffected by other performers is classified as:
questions.explain: Closed skills occur in stable, predictable environments largely unaffected by the surroundings.

questions.q: Carron's model identifies task cohesion and which other type of cohesion?
questions.explain: Carron distinguishes task cohesion (working together for goals) and social cohesion (getting along).

questions.q: Increased heart rate, sweating and muscle tension before performance are signs of:
questions.explain: Somatic anxiety refers to the physiological responses to a perceived threat or stressor.

questions.q: In Bandura's model of observational learning, the four processes are attention, retention, motor reproduction and:
questions.explain: Bandura's four stages are attention, retention, motor reproduction and motivation.

questions.q: A learner in the cognitive stage of learning is best characterised by:
options: Trial and error and frequent gross errors
questions.explain: In the cognitive stage learners form a mental picture and use trial and error, making many errors.

questions.q: Feedback that comes from within the performer via the kinaesthetic sense is called:
questions.explain: Intrinsic feedback is felt by the performer through proprioception and kinaesthesis.

questions.q: A generalised series of movements stored in long-term memory is known as a:
questions.explain: A motor programme is a generalised plan of an action stored in long-term memory.

questions.q: A leader who is appointed from outside the group by an external authority is a(n):
questions.explain: A prescribed leader is appointed from outside the group, often by a governing body or organisation.

questions.q: Information about the outcome of a movement, such as the score, is known as:
questions.explain: Knowledge of results gives information about the outcome or end product of the action.

questions.q: According to Bandura, self-efficacy is best defined as:
questions.explain: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's ability to succeed in a specific task or situation.

questions.q: Lewin's formula B = f(P x E) best supports which view of personality?
questions.explain: B = f(P x E) shows behaviour as a function of personality and environment, the interactionist view.

questions.q: A mismatch between beliefs and behaviour that can be used to change attitudes is called:
questions.explain: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort from conflicting beliefs, which can motivate attitude change.

questions.q: Catastrophe theory differs from the inverted-U theory because it predicts that high arousal causes:
options: A dramatic, sudden drop in performance
questions.explain: Catastrophe theory predicts a sudden, dramatic drop in performance when high arousal combines with cognitive anxiety.
